transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into things before they’re finished talking or deciding, and it’s starting to mess up my job and my money. I just can't seem to stop myself from interrupting or making snap decisions, and it's causing real problems with my boss and my wife. I'm just really frustrated and need to figure out why I keep doing this.
Have you noticed these patterns of impulsive behavior throughout your entire life since childhood, or did they start relatively recently?

It’s actually been there since I was a kid—back in elementary school, I was always getting notes home for blurting out answers, not staying in my seat, and being called "overactive" on my report cards. But it only started seriously messing with my job and my money about two years ago when my company sped up the production line and changed our bonus structure.
Beyond the impulsivity, do you also struggle with things like losing track of important tasks, difficulty staying organized, or frequently forgetting appointments or daily responsibilities?

No, I don't really struggle with organizing things or forgetting appointments in that way. It's more that I rush through things so fast that I make careless mistakes, like skipping steps on a checklist, while also struggling with interrupting people and just not being able to sit still.
Would you say that your primary struggle is more about difficulty sitting still and constant physical restlessness, or is it more about your impulsivity and inability to wait your turn?

Both of those are massive, constant struggles for me, as I always feel like I have a motor inside and my leg is constantly bouncing. But the impulsivity and cutting people off is definitely the primary struggle that brought me here today. That's the part that is actively doing the most damage to my marriage, my job, and our finances right now.

To clarify, when you are performing tasks, do you often find that you have trouble sustaining your attention or focus, or is your difficulty strictly limited to the impulsive urge to rush through them?

It’s definitely both, because while I feel a massive urge to rush, I also have a really hard time keeping my focus on the task in front of me. For example, on the line, my mind will drift or jump ahead, and I'll end up skipping a torque step or misreading a decimal on a gauge even when I'm trying to be careful. My head is just already on the next part before I've even finished what I'm doing.

When you think back to your childhood, were your teachers or parents more concerned about your inability to sit still and your constant physical movement, or was the primary issue your tendency to act without thinking and interrupt others?

Honestly, it was really a mix of both back in elementary school. I couldn't stay in my seat and my parents and report cards constantly labeled me as "overactive," but I also got endless notes home for blurting out answers and talking over the teacher. Both the physical restlessness and the constant interrupting were major issues for everyone.

Looking back at your childhood, would you say your hyperactive-impulsive behaviors were clearly more frequent and severe than your difficulties with sustaining attention, or were both equally prominent?

The hyperactive and impulsive behaviors were definitely much more prominent and frequent when I was a kid. The main issues back in school were me not staying in my seat, blurting out answers, and being labeled 'overactive' and 'disruptive.' Since I was smart enough to do the schoolwork, my attention itself wasn't really the main complaint back then.
